title: A Device to Prevent Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy: Detecting Peri-Ictal Body Position
official: A Device to Prevent Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy: Detecting Peri-Ictal Body Position
summary:
The goal of this study is to assess the performance of a commercial sheet sensor in determining body position after generalized tonic-clonic (GTC) seizures. If a sheet sensor could accurately detect GTC seizures, this could be a step towards autonomously repositioning patients with the aid of a smart mattress.

Primary Objective

Milestones:

Feasibility objective: Monitor 50 patients with the objective of capturing at least 20 GTCS events. Primary analytic objective: Achieve detection of anatomical landmarks with body position change within 5 seconds with an accuracy of 75% both interictally and post-GTCS.

Secondary Objective Detect the postictal prone position with an accuracy of 100%.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1\. Adults 18 years of age or older admitted to the BWH EMU with drug-resistant epilepsy, defined by the failure of at least two anti-seizure medications and a documented history of electroclinical seizures

Exclusion criteria:

1. Suspicion of functional dissociative seizures (psychogenic nonepileptic seizures)
2. Patients admitted for medication adjustment only
